theme: 3 terms on type members: shared values, shortcuts and cleanup

terms.definition: A property that belongs to the type itself, so every value of that type shares it.
terms.example: Make it a type property, so every `Game` shares one `maxPlayers`.

terms.definition: A shortcut that lets you read an item from a type with square brackets.
terms.example: Add a subscript to `Team`, so you can write `team[1]`.

terms.definition: A block of code in a class that runs just before the object is removed from memory.
terms.example: Put the cleanup in a deinitializer, so it runs when `Session` goes away.

video.title: Type Property, Subscript & Deinitializer | iOS Daily English Day 15
video.description:
Learn to talk about Swift type members: Type Property, Subscript and Deinitializer, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Type Property - A property that belongs to the type itself, so every value of that type shares it.
Subscript - A shortcut that lets you read an item from a type with square brackets.
Deinitializer - A block of code in a class that runs just before the object is removed from memory.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Day 15 of the iOS Daily English series: 3 terms a day, from Swift basics to advanced iOS.

Explain Type Property, Subscript and Deinitializer in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
타입 프로퍼티, 서브스크립트, 디이니셜라이저 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Type Property - A property that belongs to the type itself, so every value of that type shares it.
한국어: 타입 자체에 속해서 모든 값이 함께 쓰는 프로퍼티

Subscript - A shortcut that lets you read an item from a type with square brackets.
한국어: 대괄호로 타입 안의 항목을 읽게 해 주는 단축 문법

Deinitializer - A block of code in a class that runs just before the object is removed from memory.
한국어: 클래스 객체가 메모리에서 사라지기 직전에 실행되는 코드 블록

dialogue.title: The Chat class

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I need a limit of two users for every `Chat`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use a type property. Every chat shares one `maxUsers`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So a type property is not stored in each chat?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. You read it as `Chat.maxUsers`, from the type.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. Now I write `chat.names[1]` all the time. It is long.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Add a subscript. Then you can write `chat[1]`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, a subscript takes an index in square brackets, like an array?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Last thing: we must close the socket when a chat ends.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I can call a `close` method at the end of every screen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't. Put it in a deinitializer, and Swift runs it for you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. A deinitializer runs when the `Chat` object goes away.
